units.source_text: “是啊。”我答道。

en.t: "Yes," I answered.

units.source_text: 可我又一直觉得，我们主动提出这种事情，对病人是不是不太好。

en.t: But I had always felt that it might not be good for the sick man if we brought up such a matter ourselves.

units.source_text: 我们两人决定不了，便去跟叔父商量。

en.t: The two of us could not decide, so we went to consult my uncle.

units.source_text: 叔父也觉得很难办，他说：

en.t: My uncle also found it difficult to handle, and he said:

units.source_text: “若是有什么想说的，没说出来就死了，的确很遗憾，

en.t: "If he has something he wants to say and dies without saying it, that would certainly be regrettable,

units.source_text: 但是我们若是主动催他说，恐怕也不妥吧。”

en.t: but if we take it upon ourselves to urge him to speak, that may not be proper either."

units.source_text: 这个事就这么拖延下来。

en.t: And so the matter was left hanging.

units.source_text: 不多久，病人陷入了昏睡状态。

en.t: Before long, the sick man fell into a comatose sleep.

units.source_text: 一向无知的母亲，仍然以为病人在安睡，反而高兴了，还说：

en.t: My mother, knowing nothing as usual, still thought he was sleeping peacefully and was actually pleased, saying:

units.source_text: “好了，他能这么平静地睡觉，大家也轻松了。”

en.t: "Good. If he can sleep so peacefully, it is easier on everyone too."

units.source_text: 父亲常常睁开眼睛，突然问起某人怎么了。

en.t: My father would often open his eyes and suddenly ask what had happened to someone.

units.source_text: 被他问到的往往是刚才坐在他枕旁的人。

en.t: The person he asked about was often someone who had just been sitting by his pillow.

units.source_text: 在父亲的意识里，形成了混沌和明亮两部分，

en.t: In my father's consciousness, two regions had formed, one dim and confused and the other bright,

units.source_text: 那明亮的部分犹如缝在黑幕上的白线，断断续续地连接着。

en.t: and the bright parts were connected intermittently, like white thread sewn onto a black curtain.

units.source_text: 也难怪母亲把父亲的昏睡状态误认为是在安睡了。

en.t: It was no wonder that my mother mistook my father's coma for peaceful sleep.

units.source_text: 父亲说话也渐渐地含混不清了，

en.t: My father's speech also gradually became slurred,

units.source_text: 说出的话总是越往后越听不清楚，所以往往最终还是不得要领。

en.t: and his words would always become harder to hear toward the end, so we often failed to grasp what he meant.

units.source_text: 但是，父亲每次开口说话的时候，声音还挺大，完全不像是病入膏肓的人。

en.t: Yet whenever my father began to speak, his voice was still quite strong, nothing like that of a man at death's door.

units.source_text: 我们要跟他说话，却要用比平时更高的声音，凑近他耳边说才行。

en.t: When we spoke to him, however, we had to raise our voices higher than usual and bring our mouths close to his ear.

units.source_text: “给你冰着脑袋，觉得舒服些吗？”

en.t: "Does it feel better to have your head cooled with ice?"
"Mm."
